extracted.intended_audience: epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers, and journal editors involved in observational studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors and editors on improving the transparency and completeness of reporting for observational epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), including use of field-specific extensions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Statement aim
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE stands for an international, collaborative initiative of epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers and journal editors involved in the conduct and dissemination of observational studies, with the common aim of STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement provides guidance intended to improve reporting of observational studies so readers can assess strengths and weaknesses; it is developed collaboratively by relevant methodological and editorial stakeholders. (Page notes that the Statement is being endorsed by a growing number of biomedical journals and has PubMed entries.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on transparency in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational Studies: Getting clear about transparency (headline/new guidelines referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initiative highlights transparency as a core principle for reporting observational research; new guideline discussions and articles (e.g., in PLOS Medicine) reinforce that transparent reporting is a key evaluative standard for observational study reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of STROBE extensions for specific subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: STROME‑ID (Strengthening the Reporting of Molecular Epidemiology for Infectious Diseases) is cited as an extension of the STROBE statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where subfield‑specific issues arise (for example, molecular epidemiology of infectious diseases), authors should consult and apply relevant STROBE extensions to ensure domain‑specific reporting items are addressed; the site notes publication of such extensions (e.g., in Lancet Infectious Diseases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal endorsement and adoption as an evaluative signal
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE Statement is being endorsed by a growing number of biomedical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should be aware of whether their target journals endorse STROBE; endorsement implies journals expect submitted observational-study reports to adhere to STROBE reporting items and may be used as part of editorial/review assessment.
